chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Replacements: Al Gibson and Sam "The Man" Taylor
summary: McRae recommended Al Gibson and later woke Sam "The Man" Taylor to get him a job with Cab.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Al Gibson. I sent and got (Inaudible)
Was he someone who just sat in or --
Yeah. Al Gibson took -- I sent for -- he wanted a tenor player (inaudible). I say, 'Why don't yall get Al Gibson. He's a good tenor player, you know.' And they got--

Now, when he came back to New York from that trip -- when he came back from New York from that trip, he asked me -- he say he wanted a tenor player. Asked me did I want to come back with the band. I say, 'No. I'll get you a tenor player.' And I went uptown. At that time, Sam 'The
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Man" Taylor was doing a lot of -- doing some recording in his bippers but he wasn't (inaudible). He was doing some recording. He needed a job, (inaudible) something like that.
I went up to Sam "The Man" Taylor's house at 154th Street off 8th Avenue -- live up there. And I woke him up -- he was in the bed.
I say, "Look, I got a job for you. You want a job?" He say, "Yeah."
"You want to go with Cab?" He say, "Yeah."
"Well come on, get up, meet me down at Nola (inaudible) Studio. I got a job for you." And he hired Sam "The Man" Taylor. (inaudible) --
Sam "The Man" Taylor had been with Lucky Milliner for awhile, I think.
Then he took -- Sam "The Man" Taylor was a success with him. Real big. Good tenor player.
